source: My Natural Care — Practical At-Home Peripheral Neuropathy Self-Care Guide

chapters.title: Morning to Night: Your Daily Care Routine
chapters.summary: Build a simple rhythm for your day, from a comfortable morning to a calmer evening.
chapters.action: Choose a time for meals, safe movement, and checking your feet.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. When you wake up, stand slowly and notice how you feel.
2. Eat a balanced meal and follow the care plan recommended by your clinician.
3. Set aside a few minutes for gentle movement that is safe for you.
4. Throughout the day, choose varied foods and take breaks when you need them.
5. Before bed, inspect your feet, prepare for tomorrow, and wind down.

EVERYDAY TIP
You do not have to do everything at once. Start with two or three manageable habits.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
If you have a foot wound, significant balance problems, sharp pain, or weakness, adapt your routine with professional guidance.

chapters.title: At-Home Fitness: A Gentle Chair Routine
chapters.summary: Try a few light, seated movements when they are appropriate for you.
chapters.action: Begin with a short chair-based movement break, if it is safe for you.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Sit on a sturdy chair without wheels, with your back supported.
2. Breathe normally while gently rolling your shoulders backward and forward.
3. Bend and straighten your elbows without straining.
4. If your clinician has not advised against it, keep your heels down and slowly lift and lower your toes.
5. If comfortable, lift one foot at a time as though marching while seated.
6. Rest and notice how your body feels afterward.

EVERYDAY TIP
About five minutes can be a starting point. Begin with a few repetitions and increase only when safe.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
These exercises are educational examples, not a prescription. Avoid them when you have wounds, dizziness, severe pain, unsteadiness, or new symptoms without medical guidance. Stop and seek help for chest pain or unusual shortness of breath.

chapters.title: Three Seated Movements for Feet and Ankles
chapters.summary: Explore slow ankle and foot movements to support mobility when advised.
chapters.action: Try one comfortable seated movement, if appropriate for you.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Sit with your back supported and your feet on the floor.
2. Keeping your heels down, gently raise your toes, then lower them slowly.
3. Keeping the fronts of your feet down, gently raise your heels and lower them without dropping.
4. If comfortable, lift one foot slightly and make small ankle circles.
5. Rest between movements and inspect your feet afterward.

EVERYDAY TIP
You do not need to become tired. Keep every movement slow and controlled.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Ask for individualized guidance if you have wounds, significant foot deformities, new weakness, or trouble moving your feet. Icons are illustrative, not demonstrations of posture.

chapters.title: Arms and Shoulders: Move While Seated
chapters.summary: Gentle upper-body movements you can do from a stable chair.
chapters.action: Take a brief seated movement break, if comfortable.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Sit in a sturdy chair with your back supported.
2. Slowly open and close your hands without squeezing tightly.
3. Bend and straighten your elbows at a comfortable pace.
4. Gently roll your shoulders backward, then relax.
5. Stop and rest before you feel overly tired.

EVERYDAY TIP
Link this little movement break to something you already do each day.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Stop if you feel sharp pain, new weakness, dizziness, or shortness of breath. Do not add weights without advice.

chapters.title: Walking Safely Around Your Home
chapters.summary: Make short walks safer by checking the space and your feet.
chapters.action: Choose a clear, short walking route at home, if walking is safe.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Clear loose rugs, cables, and other obstacles from your path.
2. Wear comfortable, secure shoes that protect your feet.
3. Check for foot wounds or pressure spots before walking.
4. Walk slowly for a short distance and stop to rest as needed.
5. Afterward, check your balance and the skin on your feet.

EVERYDAY TIP
If walking is not safe, ask your healthcare professional about seated alternatives.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Foot wounds, falls, dizziness, substantial loss of sensation, or heart-related conditions may require an individualized activity plan.

chapters.title: Make Your Home Safer to Prevent Falls
chapters.summary: Simple changes can make everyday movement more secure.
chapters.action: Remove one tripping hazard from a frequently used area.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Keep the route between your bed, doorway, and bathroom clear.
2. Make sure you can easily turn on a light at night.
3. Remove slippery rugs and loose cords.
4. Store everyday items at heights you can comfortably reach.
5. If recommended, ask about grab bars or mobility aids.

EVERYDAY TIP
Ask someone to help move furniture or install supports. Your safety comes first.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Tell a healthcare professional about falls or near-falls. Avoid challenging balance exercises when alone.

chapters.title: A Five-Minute Daily Foot Check
chapters.summary: A practical way to look for skin changes you may not feel.
chapters.action: Set aside five minutes to inspect both feet today.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Sit somewhere with good lighting.
2. Look over the top of each foot and around the ankles.
3. Check your toes, nails, and the spaces between your toes.
4. Use a mirror or ask for help to inspect your soles and heels.
5. Look for blisters, cuts, cracks, swelling, or color changes.
6. Compare what you see with the previous day.

EVERYDAY TIP
Pair this check with changing clothes or getting ready for bed.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
If you have diabetes or reduced sensation, seek prompt professional assessment for wounds, discharge, redness, warmth, or swelling—even when there is no pain.

chapters.title: Wash, Dry, and Protect Your Feet
chapters.summary: A gentle foot-care routine that avoids unnecessary heat and friction.
chapters.action: Check how you wash, dry, and care for the skin on your feet.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Check the water temperature safely. Use lukewarm, not hot, water.
2. Wash your feet gently without harsh scrubbing.
3. Dry thoroughly, especially between your toes.
4. For dry skin, ask about an appropriate moisturizer; avoid applying lotion between the toes.
5. Do not shave calluses or cut blisters or thick skin with blades.

EVERYDAY TIP
Ask for help or professional foot care if you cannot reach your feet or trim your nails safely.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Avoid hot foot baths and never place heating pads or ice directly on areas with numbness.

chapters.title: Choose Shoes and Socks That Protect
chapters.summary: Reduce friction and pressure with a few everyday footwear checks.
chapters.action: Inspect the shoes and socks you already use.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Check inside each shoe for pebbles, foreign objects, or rough seams.
2. Make sure your toes have room and your shoes stay securely on.
3. Choose clean socks without large folds or bunching.
4. Inspect your feet after wearing new shoes.
5. If you have reduced sensation, wear suitable protective footwear indoors too.

EVERYDAY TIP
Start by adjusting what you already own before buying anything new.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
A history of ulcers, foot deformities, or repeated calluses may require professionally fitted therapeutic footwear or insoles.

chapters.title: Build a Balanced Plate at Home
chapters.summary: Put together an everyday meal with vegetables, protein, and suitable carbohydrates.
chapters.action: Make one balanced meal using familiar ingredients.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Choose a vegetable you enjoy.
2. Add a suitable protein such as eggs, fish, chicken, beans, or lentils.
3. Include rice, potatoes, or another grain or starch according to your needs.
4. Reduce sugary drinks where appropriate.
5. Plan a similar meal for another day.

EVERYDAY TIP
Rice, beans, eggs, and vegetables are practical options that can be adjusted to your nutrition plan.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Diabetes, kidney disease, allergies, and swallowing difficulties require individualized food choices. No single food cures neuropathy.

chapters.title: Simple Swaps in the Kitchen and Grocery Store
chapters.summary: Make small, realistic food changes rather than starting a restrictive diet.
chapters.action: Choose one food or drink swap that works for you.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Consider water or an appropriate unsweetened drink instead of frequent soda.
2. Choose whole fruit more often than heavily sweetened juice.
3. Add vegetables to a meal that usually has none.
4. Try a suitable fiber- or protein-containing snack instead of only sweets.
5. Plan two meals and write a short shopping list.

EVERYDAY TIP
Choose affordable, seasonal foods. You do not need a radical diet.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
If you take insulin or other medicines that can cause low blood sugar, follow medical advice when changing eating patterns.

chapters.title: Hydration: Make It Easier to Remember
chapters.summary: Use simple reminders to drink according to your personal needs.
chapters.action: Put an easy-to-use glass or water bottle somewhere convenient.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Choose a glass or bottle that is comfortable to use.
2. Link drinking to meals or regular breaks.
3. Refill your water when the container is empty.
4. When going out, plan where you can get fluids.
5. Cut back on very sugary drinks when appropriate.

EVERYDAY TIP
Make your surroundings do the reminding instead of relying only on memory.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
If you have a fluid restriction, kidney disease, or heart failure, follow your prescribed fluid limit. Do not force extra water to increase your score.

chapters.title: A Calmer Evening and Better Rest
chapters.summary: Create a gentle nighttime routine and a safer path through your home.
chapters.action: Choose a relaxing activity to repeat before bed.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Dim bright lights and reduce stimulating activities before bedtime.
2. Prepare the clothes or items you will need in the morning.
3. Try calming music or reading.
4. Breathe slowly and naturally without holding your breath.
5. Make sure the route to the bathroom is clear and lit.

EVERYDAY TIP
Similar sleep and wake times may help you build a steady routine.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Tell your healthcare professional if pain often interrupts your sleep. Avoid using alcohol to fall asleep or strong heat on numb feet.

chapters.title: Two Capsules: Remember the Correct Routine
chapters.summary: Simple ways to follow the product label without extra doses.
chapters.action: Set a safe daily reminder based on the product directions.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Read your product label and any instructions in your care plan.
2. For the product featured in this app, follow the stated guidance of two capsules per day without exceeding it.
3. If appropriate, connect the dose to a meal or another daily activity.
4. In the Care tab, mark the capsules only after you have taken them.
5. Keep a list of other medicines and supplements you use.

EVERYDAY TIP
A simple alarm can help you stay consistent.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Do not double missed doses, replace prescribed treatments, or combine duplicate ingredients without professional advice. High doses of vitamin B6 can cause neuropathy.

chapters.title: Your Weekly Calendar of Small Habits
chapters.summary: Give each day one approachable care activity.
chapters.action: Pick one small care goal for each day this week.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Monday: check your footwear and organize your schedule.
2. Tuesday: try safe seated movement, if suitable.
3. Wednesday: add vegetables to a meal.
4. Thursday: take an active break or rest as advised.
5. Friday: inspect your feet and review your sleep.
6. Saturday: repeat a habit that worked for you.
7. Sunday: celebrate progress and plan one adjustment.

EVERYDAY TIP
If a day does not go as planned, start again the next day.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Do not make up for missed days with extra capsules, strenuous exercise, or restrictive diets.

chapters.title: Your First Seven Days of Self-Care
chapters.summary: A seven-day introduction with manageable daily actions.
chapters.action: Begin with today's small task and move at your own pace.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Day 1: choose a time to check your feet.
2. Day 2: remove one tripping hazard at home.
3. Day 3: improve the balance of one meal.
4. Day 4: try appropriate gentle movement if advised.
5. Day 5: check your treatment reminders and labels.
6. Day 6: prepare a relaxing sleep routine.
7. Day 7: notice which changes you were able to maintain.

EVERYDAY TIP
Each task is an invitation, not an obligation. Replace anything that is unsuitable for you.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Skip activities that are contraindicated. Safety matters more than points.

chapters.title: Your 30-Day At-Home Care Plan
chapters.summary: A month-long framework for building habits, not a promise of recovery.
chapters.action: Choose one practical goal for your first week.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Week 1: organize your living space, foot mirror, footwear, and schedule.
2. Week 2: improve one meal and plan suitable hydration.
3. Week 3: continue safe movements that felt comfortable.
4. Week 4: review sleep, movement, and daily habits and decide what to keep.
5. Every three days: complete the optional quiz to monitor consistency.
6. At month-end: write down questions for your next health appointment.

EVERYDAY TIP
Begin small and recognize what you have already made part of your day.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
This plan does not guarantee recovery in 30 days. Progress depends on the cause of neuropathy and individual health factors.

chapters.title: Notice Your Progress and Your Symptoms
chapters.summary: Simple notes can help you see patterns and discuss them during appointments.
chapters.action: Write down one observation about how you feel today.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Record the date, location, and type of tingling, numbness, or burning.
2. If you have pain, note its intensity on a scale from 0 to 10.
3. Notice how you slept and how easily you completed everyday tasks.
4. Record any falls, wounds, or new weakness.
5. Compare several days rather than a single moment.

EVERYDAY TIP
Better sleep and greater independence are meaningful improvements too.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Lack of pain does not rule out injury to your feet. Significant changes need professional evaluation.

chapters.title: Use Your Care Score to Choose Your Next Step
chapters.summary: Turn your habit score into a small, practical action.
chapters.action: Choose one habit to improve after your next care check-in.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Open the Care tab and answer the quiz when available.
2. Think honestly about the last three days.
3. Review food, movement, foot care, sleep, hydration, and capsules.
4. Choose one manageable action in the area you want to strengthen.
5. Check in again when invited and celebrate your efforts.

EVERYDAY TIP
Select 'Not applicable' when a certain activity has not been recommended for you.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Your score tracks habit consistency, not nerve health. Never take extra capsules or do unsafe activities to raise it.

chapters.title: When Burning or Tingling Feels Uncomfortable
chapters.summary: Use safe, practical observations while following your healthcare plan.
chapters.action: Write down when symptoms appear and what may make them worse.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Note where and when symptoms started.
2. Inspect your shoes and feet for rubbing, pressure, or injury.
3. Find a comfortable position and avoid tight clothing.
4. Avoid extreme temperatures where sensation is reduced.
5. Record how you respond to recommended care and bring questions to your clinician.

EVERYDAY TIP
A quiet bedtime routine may support overall comfort.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
New weakness, wounds, a swollen or warm foot, or rapid worsening require medical attention. Do not double medicines or supplements to relieve symptoms.

chapters.title: Protect Your Hands During Household Tasks
chapters.summary: Make daily chores safer when your hands have reduced sensation.
chapters.action: Choose one tool or habit that makes household work safer.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Use appropriate protection when handling hot pans.
2. Do not test water temperature with numb hands.
3. Choose utensils with a secure, comfortable grip.
4. Take breaks if repetitive motions cause discomfort.
5. Ask for help with heavy or dangerous objects.

EVERYDAY TIP
Small adjustments can improve safety while preserving independence.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
New or progressive weakness needs a medical assessment.

chapters.title: If You Have Diabetes: Organize Your Daily Care
chapters.summary: Keep glucose monitoring, medicine, meals, and foot checks coordinated.
chapters.action: Review the care steps your diabetes team has recommended.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Check blood glucose as instructed by your healthcare team.
2. Take medications exactly as prescribed.
3. Plan meals and activity with your risk of low blood sugar in mind.
4. Inspect your feet daily if advised.
5. Record readings and symptoms to discuss at appointments.

EVERYDAY TIP
Glucose targets and testing frequency vary from person to person.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
Never change insulin or other medicines on your own. If you do not have diabetes, this chapter does not mean you need to start testing glucose.

chapters.title: Ask for Help Without Losing Independence
chapters.summary: Protect your autonomy by deciding when a little help makes activities safer.
chapters.action: Identify one task where help would improve safety.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Explain which care activities you prefer to do yourself.
2. Ask for help checking your soles if you cannot reach them.
3. Arrange company for walks if balance is a concern.
4. Keep useful items and reminders where you can reach them.
5. If helpful, bring someone to appointments to take notes.

EVERYDAY TIP
Communicate clearly and respect your limits.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
No one should force exercises, cut calluses, or treat deep wounds without professional advice.

chapters.title: Important Warning Signs: When to Get Help
chapters.summary: Know when symptoms need urgent evaluation rather than home care.
chapters.action: Keep emergency and healthcare contact information easy to find.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Seek emergency care for sudden or rapidly increasing weakness, trouble breathing, or possible stroke symptoms.
2. Seek emergency help for new loss of bladder or bowel control alongside neurological symptoms.
3. Get prompt care for wounds, discharge, or a foot that is hot, red, and swollen.
4. Report repeated falls, dizziness, or changes in foot color.
5. Do not try to manage infections or deep wounds using home remedies alone.

EVERYDAY TIP
Getting help is an important part of self-care, not a setback.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
This guide is educational and does not replace an individualized medical assessment.

chapters.title: Keep Caring for Yourself in the Months Ahead
chapters.summary: Maintain flexible, realistic care routines over the long term.
chapters.action: Choose the habits you most want to keep next month.
chapters.body:
AT-HOME STEP-BY-STEP
1. Every day: continue the recommended foot, food, and rest habits.
2. Every week: review your habits and prepare useful supplies.
3. Every month: compare notes about symptoms and activities.
4. At appointments: bring questions about treatments and lifestyle changes.
5. If anything new happens: seek guidance rather than waiting for the next monthly review.

EVERYDAY TIP
Aim for habits you can maintain, not perfection.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE
If an activity stops being appropriate for you, adjust it with a healthcare professional.
